text:
Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic summed up Buffalo's night in one line: the Sabres had more giveaways (20) than shots on goal (19). That is how a team ends up winless in five (0-4-1), and how the Flyers, who spent the first period looking a step slow, walked away with a 4-3 win that our replays say they earned. Philadelphia deserved to win 60% of the time, and outshot Buffalo 33 to 19.

It started badly for the home side. Mattias Samuelsson scored 47 seconds in, on a shot with a 5% chance of going in. From there the game turned into a trade. Jamie Drysdale tied it in the second, Tage Thompson put Buffalo back in front, and then came the goal of the night: Drysdale's long feed found its way through traffic to Owen Tippett for a tip-in. Drysdale told PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor he saw it slip past two players and thought, "Oh my gosh, this is gonna get to him."

The third belonged to the Flyers. Travis Sanheim scored 29 seconds in. Jiri Kulich answered at 4:31 off a slick setup from Thompson, a goal Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon said Kulich "really needed." Fifty-two seconds later Christian Dvorak sniped Alex Lyon, who had come out aggressively (Yerdon's read), on a shot with a 2% chance of going in, and that one stood, lifting Philadelphia's win chance from 52% to 79%. Joseph Woll's biggest save came 19 seconds later, on Jack Quinn, and kept it there.

Lyon was busy all night and finished about a goal worse than his 33 shots deserved, which tells you less about him than about the Sabres' crease all month: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen got pulled in the 8-3 loss to Tampa, Colten Ellis struggled in relief, and Lyon only just returned. Buffalo has now lost four of the five in regulation.

For the Flyers, the quiet story is Matvei Michkov, who had two assists in a week when his name has been everywhere. General manager Daniel Briere and coach Rick Tocchet have both said he never asked for a trade, and on Tuesday he looked to us like a player settling in, not one heading out.
headline: Sabres give it away, Flyers take it
